title: Skill Rooms: Proctored Work-Sample Studios for Hiring
one_liner: Walk-in, device-free testing studios where candidates take a 90-minute employer-designed work sample under ID-verified proctoring, with a portable score that many employers honor.
customer: Staffing firms and mid-size employers hiring entry and mid-level roles (customer support, analysts, junior developers, paralegals, sales development) who are drowning in AI-written applications and AI-assisted interview cheating. Employers pay $75-200 per sitting, candidates pay nothing.
problem: Resumes and cover letters are now noise. In a dataset of about 19,000 live interviews from mid-2025 to early 2026, over a third of candidates showed signs of AI-assisted cheating (close to half in software engineering). Google, Cisco and McKinsey have brought back in-person rounds, but each employer improvising its own on-site test is expensive.
solution: Studios in 10 metros, rented after hours from coworking spaces and community colleges. Fixed-time sittings with ID checks and locked-down machines, and standard job-family work samples (writing under time limit, spreadsheet modeling, code on an air-gapped machine, mock client call), scored by rubric with human review and AI assistance. Candidates get a 'Verified Work Sample' credential valid for 12 months and portable across employers, and employers receive pre-screened slates.
why_now: AI cheating in remote interviews is now measurable and widely reported, in-person verification is returning at large employers, and entry-level applicant floods make cheap, trustworthy screening valuable. Existing proctoring vendors (OnVUE and similar) focus on certification exams, not hiring work samples.
revenue_model: Per-sitting fee from employers, premium pricing for custom work samples, per-hire placement fees through staffing partners, and optional paid practice tests for candidates.
non_obvious_insight: When signals get cheap, standardized proctored tests win, which is how the SAT displaced recommendation letters. The portable score, not the room, is the business: every additional employer that honors it lowers each candidate's cost of proving skill and raises its value, and it gives displaced or credential-less workers a way to prove themselves without a degree.
first_30_days: Rent a 12-seat room in one city and sign 5 staffing agencies hiring for three roles. Design three work samples and rubrics, then run a first cohort of about 40 candidates. Charge employers $125 per candidate who passes, and use the results to sign the next 10 employers on the same score.

title: Fake-Support Scam Takedown for Fintechs
one_liner: A monitoring and takedown service that finds scammers posing as your customer support in public help threads, clusters them by phone, WhatsApp and Telegram identifiers, and kills them fast with regulator-ready evidence files.
customer: Fraud, trust & safety and CX heads at crypto exchanges, wallet makers, neobanks, BNPL and payment providers. Start with mid-market crypto/fintech ($5M-$50M ARR), then EU payment service providers. Roughly $3k-$10k per month.
problem: Every 'my account is locked' thread in a fintech or crypto subreddit gets a friendly stranger reply within minutes, then a DM pushing a WhatsApp or Telegram 'support agent'. Mods remove the comments, but the brand never sees removed comments or DMs. The same 20-50 phone numbers and handles recycle week after week, and victims are usually novices or seniors. Mods keep private spreadsheets of these identifiers, and nobody aggregates them for the brand being impersonated.
solution: Monitor public help venues (Reddit through licensed access or partners, plus X, Facebook groups, YouTube comments, Google Business listings, review-site replies and search ads) for support-impersonation patterns. Extract the contact identifiers, graph-cluster them into campaigns, and file takedowns with WhatsApp/Telegram, telcos, registrars and platforms. Produce timestamped evidence packs for refund disputes and regulators. Give each brand a pre-registered 'official support channels' beacon that community mods can add to a sticky or AutoMod reply for free, cutting victim conversion without any content moderation. Mods are never paid, and the data flows to them.
why_now: The EU PSR/PSD3 political agreement of 27 November 2025 makes payment providers refund customers in bank-employee impersonation scams and makes online platforms liable to those providers if they fail to remove notified fraudulent content. Notification evidence and takedown speed now have a dollar value. The UK's mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement (since October 2024) already priced this risk. LLM-written scam scripts are fluent, which defeats keyword filters.
revenue_model: SaaS subscription of $3k-$10k per month per brand, a per-takedown premium tier, evidence-pack retainers for payment providers in the EU, and later an identifier feed sold to telcos and platforms.
non_obvious_insight: The scam's weak point is the contact channel, not the message. Fluent AI text is cheap, but the phone numbers, handles and domains are a small recyclable set, so identifier graphs beat content classifiers. Mod removal logs also hold the ground truth on how many minutes a scam reply survives, which brands can't see and which now matters for liability. An 'official channels' sticky is the cheapest conversion-killer there is.
first_30_days: Build a free 'exposure audit' for 10 mid-size crypto and fintech brands: a 30-day scan of public threads, X and Google Business listings that shows them 40 live scam identifiers and how long each survived. Send each fraud lead their own brand's data. Convert 2 into $2.5k/month paid pilots. Partner with 3 volunteer mod teams of fintech subreddits, giving them free tooling and taking labeled ground truth in return, with no payment to mods.

title: RouteRx: Pharmacy Delivery on Co-op Fuel Routes
one_liner: Piggyback prescription and essentials delivery onto the propane, fuel and feed routes that already pass most rural households, so surviving independent pharmacies can serve people the chains just abandoned.
customer: Independent rural pharmacies (per-delivery fee), Medicare Advantage and Part D plans and rural health clinics (per-member adherence and wellness-check fee), and the co-op energy department, which keeps a share of route revenue.
problem: Rite Aid is gone, Walgreens is closing about 1,200 stores through 2027, and more than 2,000 US pharmacies closed in 2025 alone. Rural residents, especially older ones on propane and well water, are hours from a counter. Standalone courier delivery in a county of 12,000 people costs $15 to $30 a drop in deadhead miles. Independents cannot afford it, and plans cannot buy adherence in places with no last mile.
solution: The co-op's energy drivers already pass nearly every farmstead and acreage in a 25-mile radius on weekly or monthly cycles. They know the gate codes, where the dog is, and which customers live alone. Add a locked, tamper-evident tote and a driver app with signature capture and temperature logging. A partner pharmacy dispenses, and the driver acts as its contracted courier under existing Iowa delivery rules, with no controlled substances at first. Add optional 'no-heat and welfare check' notes that flag when a propane customer looks unwell, triggering a call to family or the clinic.
why_now: The 2025 to 2026 pharmacy shakeout has left rural pharmacy deserts, and Drug Channels' August 2026 analysis describes a K-shaped market of urban consolidation and rural lost access. Payers are looking for adherence and social-needs benefits. Co-op energy departments are under margin pressure and need new route revenue.
revenue_model: $5 to $9 per delivery from pharmacies. Medicare Advantage and Part D plan per-member-per-month adherence and check-in fees. The co-op takes a route revenue share of roughly 30%. Optional expansion to labs, groceries and parcels.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing in rural health is not delivery technology but route density that is already paid for. A propane bobtail passing a home every three weeks has a near-zero marginal stop cost, and it carries something no courier startup has, which is trust from decades of showing up.
first_30_days: Sign one co-op with an LP fleet and one independent pharmacy in an adjacent town that just lost a competitor. Get a written read from the Iowa Board of Pharmacy and the co-op's insurer. Run a 20-household pilot with tamper-evident bags and an off-the-shelf delivery app. Record cost per stop and refill adherence to pitch a regional Medicare Advantage plan.

title: Failed-Part Bounty for Insurance Subrogation
one_liner: Pay plumbers a bounty to bag, photograph and chain-of-custody the pipe, supply line or fitting that failed, then sell the evidence and a brand-level failure database to insurers' subrogation units and manufacturers.
customer: Subrogation departments and subro vendors at regional and mutual homeowners insurers (the ones too small to send a forensic engineer to a $9k supply-line loss). Second buyers: plumbing manufacturers, distributors and private-label buyers who license the failure data.
problem: Water damage is among the top two homeowner claim categories. Product-defect subrogation (a supply line, PEX fitting, toilet connector, ice-maker line or water heater that failed early) only works if someone kept the failed part. The plumber is on scene 1 to 3 days before the adjuster, cuts the failed piece out, and tosses it in the truck-bed scrap bin. When the adjuster arrives the evidence is gone, the insurer eats the loss, and the manufacturer's lawyers cite spoliation. Insurers only hire the $2,000 forensic engineer on the big losses, so the routine $8-15k losses are never pursued. Meanwhile every plumber knows which brands are failing (certain plastic-nut braided lines, certain fill valves, certain fitting lots) but nobody aggregates it.
solution: A 90-second protocol and kit. Tamper-evident bag with a QR label, a phone flow (photo of the part in place, photo after removal, the manufacturer stamp or date code, homeowner e-signature by text, and the claim number if one exists). A weekly courier pickup from the shop and a climate-controlled evidence locker. Optional one-page factual cause-of-loss statement drawn from the same photos (sudden burst versus long-term seepage, which is exactly the 'gradual leak' exclusion that decides whether homeowners get paid). Every part is logged by brand, model, date code and failure mode, which builds a Backblaze-style public failure-rate report by product line. Insurers get the part plus a ready evidence package. The shop gets a bounty and a small line item on the invoice.
why_now: Water-loss severity has risen sharply and carriers are under pressure on homeowners loss ratios, so they are hunting for recovery dollars. Copper and steel tariffs plus the shift to PEX and imported fittings have flooded the market with cheaper components of unknown quality. Photo and OCR tooling now makes a cheap, standardized evidence workflow possible, and the subrogation trade press is openly saying evidence preservation is the make-or-break step.
revenue_model: Insurer or subro vendor pays $75-150 per part with a documented chain of custody, of which $40-60 goes to the shop and tech. Plus a 3-8% success share on any recovery that follows. Plus annual data licenses ($15-60k) to manufacturers, distributors and big-box private-label buyers, and per-report fees for expert-witness-ready packages.
non_obvious_insight: The evidence that decides tens of millions in recoveries is currently destroyed daily by the only people who touch it first, and the reason is not malice. Nobody pays a tech to spend 4 minutes and a bag on a piece of scrap. The plumber, not the adjuster, is the true first-notice-of-loss for the product itself. The bounty is a price signal, and the dataset that falls out is one nobody else can buy.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 shops through a local PHCC chapter and the owner Facebook and peer groups with a flat $50 per bag and a free kit. Design the label and the phone flow in a form tool. Collect the first 50 parts with photos. Take the first 20 case files to two regional mutual insurers and a subrogation vendor and ask them which they would have pursued. Sell a paid pilot for 100 parts on the strength of their answers.

title: Orphan Lien Clearance Desk for Title Agents
one_liner: A flat-fee curative service that proves dead solar fixture filings and other zombie liens are dead (or gets them released) so home closings stop stalling.
customer: Independent title and escrow agencies and real estate attorneys in high-solar states (AZ, CA, FL, TX, NJ, NC, NV, CO), billed per file and usually paid by the seller at closing. Listing agents in solar-heavy markets are a second channel.
problem: Sunnova filed Chapter 11 in June 2025 (500,000+ customers), Mosaic and PosiGen followed, and the residential solar credit ended for 2026 installs, so thousands of homes carry UCC-1 fixture filings and recorded solar-lease notices held by dead, merged or reassigned entities. Title examiners flag every one. Agents can't tell who holds the debt now, whether the filing is even still legally effective, or how to get a termination, so closings slip days or weeks. The people currently serving this are consumer SEO and lead-gen sites, not the title agents who actually need it solved on a deadline.
solution: Per-file lien autopsy delivered in 48 hours. (1) Pull the recorded instrument and any continuation or termination filings from the county index and the Secretary of State. (2) Compute lapse under UCC 9-515 (five years unless continued in the six-month window). (3) Trace the assignment and servicer chain through bankruptcy dockets and servicer notices. (4) Deliver either an underwriter-ready 'lapsed, no exception' memo, or a payoff/estoppel request plus a pre-drafted termination (UCC-3, or debtor-filed termination where the statute allows) recorded in that county's required format. Recorded memoranda of lease, which do not lapse, get a release workflow instead. Later expand the same engine to satisfied-but-never-released mortgages, expired judgment liens, dead PACE liens and resurfaced zombie second mortgages.
why_now: 2025-2026 solar installer bankruptcies (Sunnova, Mosaic, PosiGen) and the end of the residential solar credit produced the largest single wave of orphaned fixture filings ever recorded. 2018-2021 installs are now hitting their five-year lapse dates just as those homes come to market. Title agents are short-staffed and want to outsource curative work, and an LLM can read county index entries and bankruptcy docket text cheaply.
revenue_model: Flat fee of about $395-$900 per cleared file, contingent on clear-to-close. Agencies with volume pay $299/month plus a reduced per-file rate. White-label API for underwriters and closing software later.
non_obvious_insight: Half the 'problem liens' in solar-heavy counties are already legally dead, but the county index never shows lapse, so examiners treat a 2019 fixture filing as live forever. Clerks watch continuation filings come in, and most small installers never filed one. The work is proof of death, not payoff. Insiders also know the recorded 'notice of lease' is a different animal that never lapses, and that a clerk must record a debtor-filed termination on its face, since the office is ministerial.
first_30_days: Offer the first five files free to 3-5 independent title agencies in Phoenix, Tampa and Sacramento. Build the lapse calculator and county-index lookups for about 10 counties. Get one regional agent underwriter to accept a standard lapse-memo format. Then price at $495 per file and ask each agency for a testimonial and two referrals to listing agents.

title: Verified-Offer Shield Against H-2A Recruitment Scams
one_liner: A WhatsApp-native registry where growers publish verifiable H-2A job offers and authorized recruiters, so workers can check any offer in seconds and growers get proof they never sanctioned a fee-charging middleman.
customer: Grower associations and large H-2A employers, plus farm labor contractors running H-2A programs, who pay per worker. Workers use it free.
problem: H-2A is scaling as the domestic workforce shrinks (over 300K visas in 2024; EPI expects growth toward 500K jobs after the Oct 2025 wage rule; the workforce reportedly fell by at least 155,000). Fake recruiters and impersonated grower pages sell nonexistent jobs or charge illegal fees. H-2A rules make employers contractually responsible for banning recruiter fees, so a scam in a grower's name is a compliance and reputation hit. Late or absent arrivals mean unharvested crops.
solution: Growers verify their business identity once, attach a DOL job-order number and issue a signed offer card with a QR and short code. Recruiters receive a 'licensed by grower' credential. A worker-side WhatsApp and SMS bot works in Spanish and through voice notes for Indigenous-language speakers (Mixtec, K'iche'). It replies 'verified', 'not found' or 'fee reported' and takes fee complaints. Growers get an audit trail of their recruiter chain and arrival tracking.
why_now: The immigration crackdown removed workers, and strawberry and almond growers reportedly lost up to 30% of crews in early 2026. The H-2A wage rule changed the incentives. AI makes fake job pages, voices and documents cheap. WhatsApp Business APIs are mature, and nobody in agriculture has a verification layer.
revenue_model: $15-40 per worker per season paid by the employer or association, a premium tier for recruiter-chain audit trails and DOL-ready records, and possible lender or insurer sponsorship.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is the grower, not the victim. Growers carry the legal and commercial exposure to recruiter fraud and have the budget, while workers cannot pay. Verification for the poor is funded by the party with compliance liability.
first_30_days: Sign one grower association for a pilot with 3 member farms. Build the WhatsApp bot on the Meta Cloud API. Recruit 2-3 recruiter partners in Mexico and Guatemala. Collect 20 real scam examples through worker centers and legal-aid groups, and use them to demonstrate detection.

title: Satellite Settlement Radar for Condo Buildings
one_liner: Use free satellite radar archives to give condo boards a 10-year movement history of their building, and turn it into litigation-grade evidence when a neighboring construction project caused the settlement.
customer: Florida condo associations and property managers (3+ story buildings under post-Surfside milestone and reserve-study rules), structural engineers doing milestone inspections (white-label), buyers' agents, lenders and insurers.
problem: Milestone inspections and reserve studies are snapshots, while settlement is a trend. Boards face assessments of $30k to $100k+ per unit and don't know whether nearby construction is moving their building. A University of Miami-led study of Sentinel-1 data found subsidence of up to 8 cm in the Sunny Isles and Surfside area between 2016 and 2023 and linked it to nearby construction, yet no local product turns that into building-level reports for boards.
solution: A six-page Settlement Screening Report per building. Run open-source InSAR pipelines on Sentinel-1 (and newer radar sources) for large-footprint or tall buildings, overlay neighboring construction permits and pile-driving dates, and flag movement trends and differential settlement. Engineers can rely on it as a screening input. Optional monthly monitoring, and a litigation package with a geodesy expert declaration for claims against adjacent developers.
why_now: Post-Surfside laws now force inspections and funded reserves, so boards are spending on engineers. Free multi-year radar archives and mature open-source processing (ASF HyP3, MintPy) mean a two-person team can process buildings retroactively. Incumbents (engineers, inspectors, insurers) have not integrated satellite evidence.
revenue_model: $750 to $2,500 per building per year, $300 wholesale per building for engineering partners, monitoring subscriptions, and contingency or expert fees on construction-damage claims.
non_obvious_insight: The archive already recorded the history, so on day one you can hand a board a decade of movement. The money is in the claim, not the report: construction-induced settlement is an insurable, litigable harm, and radar time series with permit overlays date the cause. Sell the report as the intake funnel for claim work with construction-defect counsel.
first_30_days: Process 50 buildings along the Miami Beach to Sunny Isles corridor with open tools and publish a free hotspot map. Contact 100 condo boards and 10 structural engineering firms. Sell five reports at $750 and sign one construction-defect litigator as a partner. Note the limits (resolution favors large buildings) in every report.

title: Install Clubs: Brazilian Consórcio for Home Contractors
one_liner: A contractor-anchored, interest-free buying pool: 60-200 homeowners pay monthly into escrow and each month a few move up the queue (by draw or bid) to get their roof, heat pump or solar+battery installed.
customer: Independent home-service contractors (roofing, HVAC/heat pump, solar+storage, windows) with 5-50 staff who want pre-sold backlog. Their end users are homeowners who have been quoted $8-20k and don't want a 9-12% HELOC or home-improvement loan.
problem: Big-ticket home upgrades stall on financing. Contractors burn 10-20% of revenue on lead gen and lose many quoted jobs because the homeowner can't or won't borrow. The 25C/25D federal credits ended for installs after Dec 31, 2025, so the effective price jumped overnight.
solution: Software + bank escrow + a lawyer-drafted prepaid-service template that lets a contractor run a 'club' for one product (e.g., a $9k heat-pump install). Members pay $100-200/month into segregated escrow. Every month one or more members are allocated an install by lottery or by bidding extra to jump the queue. The contractor is the counterparty and delivers at a locked price, so there is no loan and no interest. The platform earns an administration fee instead of interest, as Brazilian consórcios do.
why_now: Brazil's consórcio system hit a record 12.76M active participants and about R$500B of credit sold in 2025, in a high-rate environment, so the model is proven when loans are expensive. In the US the 25C/25D credits vanished on Dec 31, 2025, rates are still high, and the only consórcio-style player I found (NWX) sells general credit letters for real estate and vehicles. Nobody has wrapped the pool around a service the seller delivers.
revenue_model: Administration fee of roughly 8-12% of contract value collected in monthly installments, a SaaS fee per contractor club, and a share of escrow float yield.
non_obvious_insight: A consórcio is not a loan, it is a queue with a price guarantee. Making the licensed contractor the counterparty turns the pool into a prepaid-service escrow (like layaway) instead of a credit product, which sidesteps most lending regulation. The contractor gets what it wants most: scheduled backlog, cash before work, and near-zero CAC because 'your neighbor's roof gets done this month' recruits the next member. Homeowners who were declined or scared off by loans are the fastest-filling segment.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 contractors in one state. Get an escrow account at a community bank and a prepaid-service agreement drafted by a lawyer who knows that state's home-improvement deposit rules. Mine each contractor's list of past quotes that never closed and pre-enroll about 40 members in a 'Founders Club' at about $150/month for a $9k install. Run the first allocation in month 2, so the first installed job and first admin-fee revenue land by around day 60.

title: Agent-Access Terms Index for Enterprises
one_liner: A living database and alert feed of what the top 500 SaaS and data vendors allow, meter and prohibit when your AI agents touch their APIs and data.
customer: General counsel, procurement and IT platform leads at 100-5,000 employee companies deploying agents, plus their outside counsel. SaaS vendors are a later customer.
problem: Most insiders read the Ninth Circuit ruling (the user, not the agent vendor, accessed Amazon) as 'agents can roam free'. For enterprises it means the fight moves to contract, and the user's company is the bound party. Vendors are already moving. SAP restricts third-party AI agent access to its APIs, Slack has throttled non-Marketplace apps and banned persistent indexes, and ServiceNow throttles inbound agent traffic. Vendors are also adding agent-action meters. No one tracks any of this, so a company can breach terms at a dozen vendors and learn about it from a suspension or audit letter.
solution: Build a structured agent-use rights matrix for about 500 vendors: allowed, banned or priced, rate limits, indexing, retention and training clauses, and official connector alternatives. Add change detection on terms and API policy pages with plain-English diffs. Add a connector that maps your OAuth-connected apps and agent inventory to the matrix and flags conflicts. Include a clause library, negotiation playbooks and an audit-defense pack.
why_now: Platform lockdowns (SAP, Slack, ServiceNow) and per-agent-action pricing arrived in 2025-26, and the Ninth Circuit ruling (August 2026) made contract the main battleground. Amazon can still seek rehearing, which adds uncertainty buyers want tracked.
revenue_model: $1.5-5k/month subscriptions for legal and procurement teams, $8-25k fixed-fee exposure reviews and negotiation packages, and later vendor-side benchmarking.
non_obvious_insight: Contract terms are becoming the price list and permission system of the agent economy, and they sit in unstructured legalese nobody indexes. The index is also the negotiating leverage, because it shows a buyer what comparable vendors concede.
first_30_days: Have an LLM plus a contract lawyer parse the terms and API policies of the top 100 SaaS vendors. Publish a free Agent Rights Scorecard for 25 of them to generate inbound. Sign 5 design partners at $1.5k/month and offer a $8-15k agent contract exposure review.

title: Sole-source price-reasonableness memos from council agenda data
one_liner: A buy-side benchmark built from public council packets showing what other governments pay Tyler, Axon, OpenGov and Flock, sold as the missing price-reasonableness memo for every sole-source renewal.
customer: Finance directors, IT directors, purchasing officers and clerks in cities and counties of 5k-250k renewing proprietary software (ERP, permitting, body cameras, ALPR). They pay $495-$1,500 per renewal brief or $3k/year subscription. Councilmembers who want a sanity check are the second audience.
problem: Vendors keep pricing confidential, and sole-source renewals sail through with no comparison. Steuben County, NY approved a five-year Tyler MUNIS/Enterprise renewal at $287,644 in 2026/27 rising 5% a year to $349,633, and the record shows no benchmarking or alternatives (5-0 vote, July 14, 2026). Danbury, CT renewed OpenGov ($71,490.65) and Tyler MUNIS ($299,274.89) unanimously as sole-source because each vendor 'is the developer of proprietary systems' (Aug 5, 2026). In National City, CA a councilmember balked at a $250,000 Tyler budgeting module ('It is a $250,000'), the public questioned the sole-source, and the council demanded a white paper with precise terms and fees.
solution: Continuously ingest agenda packets from the big agenda platforms (Legistar, Granicus, CivicClerk, CivicPlus AgendaCenter) and use LLM extraction to build a structured contract table: vendor, product, price, term, escalator, termination clause, and normalized unit metrics (per capita, per seat, per officer, per camera). Anyone facing a renewal enters the vendor and product and gets a one-page brief within a day. It gives the comparable set, the median escalator, the clauses other governments got (price caps, termination for convenience, data-export rights) and a draft sole-source price-reasonableness paragraph the purchasing officer can attach to the staff report. Later: optional negotiation support on success fee.
why_now: Multi-year Tyler and other vendor contracts are coming up for renewal in 2026, and budgets are squeezed by federal cost shifts (SNAP admin share rising to 75% in October 2026) and grant uncertainty. Agenda packets are now machine-readable at scale. Cheap LLM extraction turns a decade of scattered PDFs into a price table, which was not economically possible before.
revenue_model: $495-1,500 per renewal brief; $3k/year unlimited briefs for a county; 15% of first-year savings for negotiated renewals. Secondary revenue: a quarterly 'what governments pay' index for councils and state associations of counties.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce item is not the data, it is a price-reasonableness determination. Sole-source is only defensible when the buyer can document that the price is reasonable, and none of these records shows one. The public packets already contain the answer, and every vendor claims pricing is confidential while its own contracts are posted in agenda PDFs. Evidence: Steuben County renewal, no alternatives documented (https://citizenportal.ai/articles/9150000/new-york/steuben-county/finance-secures-fiveyear-renewal-pricing-for-munisenterprise-erp-committee-approves); Danbury sole-source renewals (https://citizenportal.ai/articles/8951200/connecticut/fairfield/danbury-city/board-renews-opengov-and-tyler-munis-contracts-totaling-roughly-370000); National City council asking for the terms and fees (https://citizenportal.ai/articles/9526083/california/san-diego-county/national-city/council-asks-city-manager-for-white-paper-after-tyler-technologies-budgeting-demo). Elko's five-year Axon extension at about $91,200 a year is another comparable data point (https://citizenportal.ai/articles/7804457/nevada/elko-county/elko-city/elko-approves-five-year-axon-contract-for-body-cameras-and-redaction-software-to-clear-backlog).
first_30_days: Scrape agenda packets from 300 mid-size jurisdictions in 2 states and extract about 500 contracts for 5 vendors. Publish a free 'What governments actually pay Tyler' leaderboard to earn inbound. Identify contracts expiring in 6-9 months from the term dates in old packets and email those finance directors a free sample brief. Sell the first 10 briefs at $495. Get 2 governments to attach the memo to a staff report as a proof point.

title: Weaver Ant Crews for Cashew and Mango Orchards
one_liner: Orchard pest control by living ant colonies: trained local 'ant agents' seed, feed and maintain weaver ants in smallholder cashew and mango trees, and the farmers get paid a residue-free premium.
customer: Smallholder cashew and mango cooperatives in Vietnam, Tanzania and West Africa, and the processors and exporters who need residue-free nuts and fruit.
problem: Smallholders spray expensive pesticides to fight coconut bugs, mirids and thrips. Costs are high, farmer health suffers, and exporters worry about residue limits. Biological control from imported predators is out of reach for smallholders.
solution: Weaver ants (Oecophylla smaragdina and O. longinoda) are territorial predators that guard trees against most pests. Our agents seed colonies, connect tree crowns with rope bridges, and supply sugar and protein supplements in the dry season. Cooperatives sign a per-tree, per-season contract. A phone-based check of nest counts and canopy occupancy generates a verified 'pesticide-free days' record that supports premium pricing with buyers.
why_now: Field research already supports it. In Vietnamese mixed pomelo and orange plantations, lower costs from ant treatments produced profit gains of 47% over pesticide plots. Economic studies of African weaver ants exist for Tanzanian cashew, and Vietnamese cashew smallholders (more than 200,000 households) are pesticide-dependent. What is new is cheap phone-based computer vision to verify colony presence, and buyers tightening residue limits.
revenue_model: A per-tree, per-season service fee set below current spray spend, plus a share (for example 10-15%) of any quality or premium uplift negotiated with exporters. Buyers can also pay a per-tonne residue-free supply fee. Ant-agent franchises would scale the model through local micro-entrepreneurs.
non_obvious_insight: Weaver ants were the world's first documented biocontrol, used in Chinese citrus groves for about 1,700 years. They never scaled because no one can patent or sell a colony, so there was no way to capture the value. The business is not the ant; it is the service wrapper, the verification data and the offtake contract that let someone get paid for a free natural crew.
first_30_days: Sign one cooperative in a cashew belt (Binh Phuoc in Vietnam or Mtwara in Tanzania). Recruit and train 20 farmers and 3 ant agents. Seed 500 trees in a pilot and compare pesticide spend and nut quality on matched control rows. Ask one processor to pre-commit to a residue-free premium.

title: Film Camera Repair Guild and Parts Mill
one_liner: A training-plus-parts network that multiplies the number of people able to repair 1970s-90s film cameras, using 3D-printed and machined parts and paid video teardown courses.
customer: Independent repair techs and serious hobbyists (parts kits and courses), used-camera shops and labs (bulk repaired-and-warrantied stock), and consumers via mail-in.
problem: The film revival is real but repairers are retiring (ABC News Dec 2025; PetaPixel Jan 2026), many now refuse to service certain models, and mechanical parts are hard to source. Dead cameras mean lost film buyers.
solution: Start with the ~25 most popular bodies (AE-1, K1000, X-700, FM2 and similar). Sell light-seal, mirror-bumper and foam kits plus printed or CNC-machined gears. Publish paid step-by-step repair courses, certify guild repairers, route overflow mail-in jobs to them, and sell warrantied repaired stock wholesale to used shops.
why_now: The retirement wave is now documented in mainstream press. Cheap multi-material printing and on-demand metal parts vendors exist. Film demand keeps rising among under-35s, and used-camera prices are climbing.
revenue_model: Parts kits ($8-40), course subscriptions (~$20/month), a ~25% share of routed repairs, and wholesale of repaired cameras with warranty.
non_obvious_insight: Film-industry insiders assume the constraint on the revival is film stock and new cameras. It is repair capacity: repair knowledge is tacit and walking out the door. Apprenticeship packaged as content, plus a parts supply, is the picks-and-shovels play, and every dead SLR is a lost film customer.
first_30_days: Buy 20 broken AE-1 and K1000 lots on eBay and film every teardown. Sell foam and seal kits on Etsy and eBay with instructions. Pre-sell 100 lifetime course seats to r/AnalogCommunity. Recruit 3 retiring techs as paid instructors on revenue share.

title: Renewal-Match Agent for Concession-Market Renters
one_liner: An agent that tracks true net-effective rents nearby, negotiates a renewal match with the landlord's leasing bot, and moves you if they refuse, paid only on savings.
customer: Renters in concession-heavy markets (Austin, Atlanta, Dallas, Phoenix, Florida) on 12-month leases, with destination landlords paying locator fees on moves.
problem: New tenants get free months while renewing tenants often receive above-market quotes, a loyalty tax. Concessions hit 15.8% of stabilized units (Austin 37%), and renters cannot see net-effective rent or spare the time to shop.
solution: With permission, the agent monitors net-effective prices in comparable buildings via listings and leasing-agent chats. About 100 days before renewal it sends a 'match or we move' letter with evidence and negotiates with the landlord's AI. If declined, it books tours, handles the move and collects the locator fee from the new building.
why_now: Operators now deploy AI leasing agents that can answer instantly, and agent protocols (like MCP-style interfaces) are appearing in property platforms. At 34 days to lease, landlords want to avoid turnover.
revenue_model: 25% of first-year renewal savings, locator commission from destination landlords on moves (often 50-100% of a month's rent in Texas and Georgia), and a premium lease-vault tier.
non_obvious_insight: Rental pricing has the same new-customer-discount, loyal-customer-premium structure that made insurers and telcos vulnerable to automated switching. When both sides run machines, the price reflects true clearing rather than inertia.
first_30_days: Run a manual concierge for 50 Austin renters recruited from local subreddits and apartment groups, taking 25% of savings. Log every quote and outcome and publish an 'Austin loyalty tax index' to attract more.

title: Sponsor-Paid Care Network for Canine Trials
one_liner: Biotechs pay for dogs' cancer care in exchange for clean, immune-competent efficacy data, solving pet-owner affordability and drug-developer validation at once.
customer: Clinical-stage biotechs (including AI-drug-discovery companies) and animal-health developers that need cheap in vivo efficacy and safety signals pay per enrolled dog. General-practice and specialty clinics are site partners. Foundations can co-fund.
problem: 85% of vet professionals say clients decline care at estimates of $1,000 or less, and about 80% of dogs with lymphoma never receive IV chemo. On the other side, AI-designed drugs are bottlenecked by assays and validation, mouse models predict poorly, and FDA's Sept 21, 2026 rule makes sponsors show that non-animal methods are 'adequately validated'. Spontaneous tumors in pet dogs (lymphoma, osteosarcoma, mast cell, bladder cancer) are well-established human-relevant models, yet trials struggle to recruit because the dogs are first seen in general practices.
solution: A network of 30-60 general practices plus a few specialty centers. AI trial-matching runs over practice-management data and an owner-facing trial finder. Sponsors fund a standard-of-care baseline (diagnostics and supportive care) so owners get treatment free. The studio handles owner consent, GCP-style data capture, INAD/CVM paperwork, and opt-in blood and tissue banking. Start with observational registries and PK/PD window studies of oral and repurposed generic drugs, then move to sponsor-funded interventional studies.
why_now: AI-biotech funding is over $6B in 2026 and sponsors are hunting for validation evidence. FDA's Sept 2026 rule and its 25-use-case NAM database push developers away from lab animals without banning them. Duffield ($250M) and PetSmart Charities are funding 'access to care', so grant co-funding for clinics is available. Oral options like Laverdia now make community-level oncology treatable.
revenue_model: $15-30k per enrolled dog (treatment, site fees, monitoring, data), at roughly 30% gross margin. $100-250k per observational registry or PK window study. Foundation grants subsidize owner-side costs.
non_obvious_insight: Pet trials fail on recruitment and owner cost, not on science. The general-practice vet is where 90% of cases first appear, and no one connects them to sponsors. Turning a sponsor's development budget into owners' treatment budgets solves the affordability crisis and delivers a data product for drug developers.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 clinics and one board-certified oncologist as scientific lead. Pitch 10 biotechs on a $100-200k canine lymphoma real-world-outcomes registry or a dog PK window study of a repurposed oral drug. Co-apply for a foundation grant to cover owner costs. Keep the first studies observational or extra-label to stay clear of the heavier INAD requirements. First revenue in about 4-6 months.

title: Real-Factory Credentials From Customs Shipping Records
one_liner: Turn public US import records into supplier-owned reputation credentials and audit-ready reasonable-care dossiers that prove a factory is a real manufacturer.
customer: Small and mid-size US importers of record (Amazon and Shopify brands, furniture, hardware and apparel distributors) re-sourcing to Vietnam, India, Mexico and Turkey. Customs brokers are a channel, and factories are the second payer.
problem: The importer of record is investigated first, and liability turns on whether it exercised reasonable care about the supplier's origin claims. In August 2026 the White House published a report on transshipment, a 40% penalty tariff applies, and CBP has expanded inspections of shipments from Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Mexico. Small importers cannot tell a real factory from a trading company or a re-labeller, and sourcing agents' claims are unverifiable.
solution: Supplier Proof. Build a profile per factory from three or more years of US import records (shipper and consignee names, volumes, product codes, ports, cadence) plus corporate registry and location data, flag anomalies such as volume beyond plausible capacity, mismatched product codes or shell-company addresses, and add optional local inspector visits. Factories claim and verify their profile and can consent to name repeat buyers as references. The output is a dossier the importer can hand to a broker or to CBP.
why_now: Tariff enforcement moved in 2025-26 from headline rates to origin verification, and the August 2026 transshipment report has put importer liability on every compliance officer's desk. Sourcing shifts away from China are happening now, so millions of dollars of orders are going to unfamiliar factories.
revenue_model: Importer subscriptions of $149-499 per month, $150-400 per dossier, inspector visits passed through at a margin, and $600-1,200 per year from factories for a verified credential once importers demand it.
non_obvious_insight: Import records are the only unforgeable cross-border reputation ledger for factories, but they are sold as raw rows to analysts. Repackaged as supplier-owned credentials with a reasonable-care wrapper, a data product becomes a compliance product with a real budget line: avoiding a 40% penalty.
first_30_days: Buy 12 months of import records for two categories (for example furniture and hardware from Vietnam and India). Auto-build about 1,000 factory profiles and hand-audit 20. Send 200 emails to sourcing managers and customs brokers. Sell the first 10 dossiers at $250 each and use them to refine the scoring.

title: Neighborhood Block Wildfire Cover via HOAs
one_liner: Softer reinsurance isn't reaching homeowners, so aggregate a mitigated neighborhood into one certified risk that capital will price like a portfolio instead of 300 anonymous parcels.
customer: HOA boards and Firewise-style communities of 200-2,000 homes in wildfire states (CA, CO, UT, NM, OR) where members are being nonrenewed or pushed to FAIR plans.
problem: Nonrenewals are at records and carriers price parcel by parcel, ignoring community-level mitigation like hydrants, vegetation control, ember vents and evacuation routes. Reinsurance is softening (Jefferies expects declines through 2027) but primary policyholders see none of it.
solution: Community risk certification, drone-verified and re-certified annually, plus block placement with an MGA or coverholder writing group-rated homeowner policies backed by reinsurance or ILS capital. The HOA collects dues, funds a shared deductible reserve and enforces mitigation standards.
why_now: California passed three claims and nonrenewal bills on 2026-09-03. Cat bond issuance is a record $18.9B year to date. Softening means capital is abundant and looking for well-defined books, and nonrenewals are a midterm political flashpoint.
revenue_model: MGA commission of about 12-15% of premium, $40-$100 per home for certification, and an HOA subscription for compliance tracking.
non_obvious_insight: In a soft market capital is abundant, and what's scarce is a verifiable, homogeneous risk pool. An HOA is a ready-made legal aggregator with dues collection and enforcement powers, which solves distribution and adverse selection together.
first_30_days: Approach 20 HOA management companies and Firewise sites in California foothills and Colorado's Front Range. Offer a free community risk-certification report. Sign one pilot LOI and line up an MGA willing to quote a block program.

title: Recipient-Priced Inboxes for Outbound Agents
one_liner: A gateway that lets busy people set a price to reach them and makes outbound AI agents bid for attention, refunding the bond when the message proves relevant.
customer: Outbound agents (fundraising, PR, recruiting sourcing, partnership and research-interview agents) that decide per message whether a reply is worth $1-$50 and pay a refundable bond. The recipient side is VC partners, journalists, podcast bookers, specialist physicians and procurement heads.
problem: Agents remove the cost of sending, so high-value inboxes are drowning. Generic AI outreach now gets under 1% replies in most B2B segments, and reaching one buyer takes 7+ touches. Filters are an arms race, and recipients earn nothing for their attention.
solution: The recipient sets a price ladder (for example $5 for a read-guarantee, $25 for a reply window) and rules. Unknown senders get an auto-reply, or an HTTP 402 for agents, carrying a payment link. The sender agent estimates expected value from its own conversion data and posts a refundable bond over MPP, x402 or card. With one tap the recipient marks the message relevant, which returns the bond, or irrelevant, which pays the recipient. We take 15-20% of forfeited bonds. Sender reputation lowers prices for good senders and prices out spammers.
why_now: Agentic outbound exploded in 2026, with agents choosing targets and follow-ups on their own and degrading deliverability. Programmatic micropayment rails now make a $2 bond collectible without a human. Recipients are actively looking for ways to filter AI outreach.
revenue_model: 15-20% of forfeited bonds plus a 5% fee on settled reads. Team-inbox and executive-assistant tiers for recipients, and an API plan for senders that want reputation scores.
non_obvious_insight: Pay-to-email has failed for 25 years because humans underprice their own outreach and hate friction. Agents compute expected value per message, so a price signal finally clears the market, and it only works when both sides are software. Letting the recipient earn money flips their incentive from blocking to hosting.
first_30_days: Build a Gmail and Chrome extension with an auto-reply rule and recruit 50 investors, journalists and podcast bookers through founder networks. Recruit 10 outbound-agent tools (fundraising, PR, recruiting) as senders. Settle bonds manually via Stripe at first and measure reply-quality uplift against free outreach. Charge the take rate from month 2.

title: Outsourced Elder-Exploitation Desk for Credit Unions
one_liner: A managed service where trained specialists take flagged older-member transactions, call the member and trusted contact, file reports and document compliance.
customer: Community banks and credit unions ($300M-$5B in assets) with older memberships. Sales run through CUSOs, state leagues and core-processor marketplaces to BSA and fraud officers.
problem: Americans 60+ reported $7.7B in fraud losses in 2025 (up 59%), with an average loss over $38k and 12,400+ people losing $100k or more. Small institutions have alerts but no trained humans to call members, coordinate lawful holds, file SARs and APS reports, and prove Senior Safe Act training.
solution: Ingest the institution's flagged-alert queue and staff a desk with retired bank fraud investigators and social workers who use scripts to break the scam spell (pig-butchering, crypto-ATM, impostor). The desk coordinates holds, files APS and SAR narratives, runs annual Senior Safe Act training, and delivers quarterly avoided-loss analytics.
why_now: Investment and pig-butchering fraud is over a third of losses, older adults are adopting AI fast (23% of 65+ use ChatGPT, up from 10%), and voice-cloning scams raise stakes. State attorneys general and regulators are pressing institutions to do more.
revenue_model: $2-6k a month per institution by asset size, plus per-case fees, sold on documented avoided loss.
non_obvious_insight: Consumer fraud apps are crowded, but the institution is the party with a duty of care, and the missing capacity is human case handling, not another detection model. Pricing to avoided losses makes the ROI obvious.
first_30_days: Sell a 90-day pilot to two credit unions through a CUSO or state league, staffed by two retired fraud investigators and a social worker. Record prevented losses and hold-to-report cycle time.

title: Dry-Hole Atlas for Hydrogen, Helium, Geothermal
one_liner: Re-read a century of scanned well logs and gas analyses, once treated as junk, to find natural hydrogen, helium and hot rock, and sell the resulting atlas to exploration companies by area of interest.
customer: Junior exploration companies and VC-backed developers in natural hydrogen, helium and geothermal (and lithium-brine plays), plus land and mineral-lease advisors who need leads. They pay for subscriptions and area-of-interest data packs.
problem: The US has millions of drilled wells. Old records include gas analyses, bottom-hole temperatures, water chemistry and mud-log shows, mostly recorded as incidental noise by oil and gas operators. They sit as scanned TIFFs and PDFs at state geological surveys and core repositories. New subsurface commodities need exactly this once-discarded information. Oil-and-gas data vendors index hydrocarbon fields, not hydrogen, helium or heat, and small explorers cannot afford to hire teams to dig through archives across 30 state surveys.
solution: A scan-to-structured-data pipeline across public state survey archives. Extract gas composition (hydrogen, helium, nitrogen), bottom-hole temperature and depth, and brine chemistry. Geolocate every record, correct for known temperature-log biases, and publish a queryable map atlas with prospectivity layers per township or section. Sell by area of interest. Offer custom queries such as 'every well within 20 miles of this substation with more than 0.3% helium and temperature above 150 C at 3 km'.
why_now: AI data centers are driving huge demand for clean firm power, and geothermal developers are raising large rounds and signing hyperscaler offtakes. Natural hydrogen exploration has attracted venture money and government attention. Helium supply has been unstable and prices volatile. Vision-language models now extract tables from old scans cheaply, and state surveys are increasingly open to releasing data.
revenue_model: Subscriptions of 15-50k USD per year per company for a basin or state atlas, area-of-interest packs of 5-25k USD, custom data services, and, later, small overriding royalties or success fees on leases won using the data.
non_obvious_insight: The value of data flips when the target commodity changes. A well that reported 'gas contains 40% hydrogen' in 1935 was a dud then, and it is a discovery lead today. Every incumbent data vendor is organized around the old commodity, so nobody re-reads the archive for byproducts. The archives are public and low-margin for the state agencies that hold them, so the moat is the extraction pipeline, cleaning and geological calibration, not data access.
first_30_days: Pick one state survey with well-documented public scans and gas-analysis reports and one target commodity (helium or hydrogen shows are the easiest to demo). Build a proof-of-concept map for one basin using a few thousand well records. Cold-email about 30 junior exploration companies and geothermal developers with the map and one concrete lead they can check. Sell 3-5 area-of-interest packs at around 5k USD each, and ask for pre-payment for the next state.

title: Payee-Verification Network for the Live Music Business
one_liner: A shared, industry-vouched directory of who is really entitled to be paid in the touring economy (agencies, promoters, venues, production vendors), checked before every deposit wire.
customer: Independent and mid-size booking agencies, regional promoters, festivals, tour accountants and business managers, and production, trucking and staging vendors. Starting wedge is 50-200 person agencies and promoters that wire 50% artist deposits.
problem: Live touring runs on large advance wires: artist-guarantee deposits, production advances and vendor prepayments, with banking details passed through PDF contracts and email across dozens of small counterparties whose bookers, agents and accountants change often. That is ideal business-email-compromise territory (US BEC losses $3.05B in 2025 per FBI IC3), and now voice clones make 'the agent called to change the account' credible (a vendor report claims 680% year-over-year growth in voice-deepfake attacks). The FBI fund-freeze process recovered 58% of attempted funds but only when victims act fast, and each bank sees only its own side. Europe's mandatory Verification of Payee on euro transfers (from Oct 2025) checks name against IBAN only inside the euro zone, and the US has nothing similar, while tours mix currencies and countries.
solution: Verify each entity once (KYB, identity of authorised signers, bank account proven by micro-deposit or open banking) and publish signed payment instructions. Settlement spreadsheets and accounting tools check payees against the network before a wire is released, via a plug-in for spreadsheets, Slack and common accounting software. Any change of banking details triggers out-of-band, multi-party confirmation (agent, manager and accountant, never a reply-to email), with a 24-72 hour cooling-off for first payments. A bank hot-line handshake speeds recall and freeze on suspected misdirection. Each deal also generates a shared verbal code phrase to defeat cloned-voice calls.
why_now: IC3's 2025 numbers, AI-enabled scam operations earning about 4.5x more than others (Chainalysis, per briefing), and cheap voice cloning. Live Nation's $25.2B revenue and its arena buying show the sector's money is growing and consolidating, so more wires move through more small counterparties. EU Verification of Payee shows regulators' direction but leaves the cross-border and hybrid gap open.
revenue_model: SaaS of $99-499/month per verified entity. Per-payment verification fee of $2-5 or 0.02-0.05% for high-value wires. Bank and payments-provider licensing. Insurance partnerships where crime/cyber insurers discount premiums for network members.
non_obvious_insight: Payments-fraud vendors sell to banks and large corporates, but the live industry is thousands of small counterparties whose trust is relationship-based. The relationship graph (who is the legitimate agent, manager or accountant for whom) lives in people's heads, so the moat is a graph the industry vouches for itself. Once most deposits flow through the network, an unverified change-of-details request becomes an obvious red flag.
first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 mid-size booking agencies or tour accountants (the people whose wires get hit). Give them a free payment-instruction registry as a spreadsheet plus Slack or Chrome extension. Capture verified bank details for their top 100 counterparties. Run a consented voice-clone fire drill to create urgency. Charge $199/month per agency by day 60 and approach two insurers for premium-discount pilots.

title: Third-Party Maintenance for Orphaned Robots
one_liner: Like third-party server maintenance for IT, a spares-and-support contract for robots whose makers failed, were acquired or stopped supporting them.
customer: 3PLs, retailers, hospitals and factories running AMRs, storage systems and delivery robots that are out of warranty or whose vendors are gone, plus lenders and bankruptcy trustees holding stranded assets.
problem: Robotics funding is concentrating (Skild $14B, Physical Intelligence $11B, Figure $39B) while the long tail starves. Agility is pivoting toward wheels, and Serve's roughly $1.3k revenue per robot signals shakeout. Buyers can be left with multimillion-dollar fleets without updates or parts.
solution: Buy stranded inventory and spares from failed vendors, arrange source-code escrow or reverse-engineer key consumables, and offer annual per-robot support contracts with SLAs. Also sell certified refurbished units.
why_now: The 2025-26 funding boom is producing its first wave of failures and consolidation, while Amazon (1M+ robots, building its own robot factory) and Symbotic ($2.25B 2025 revenue) centralize the market. The orphan pool is growing now.
revenue_model: $1.5-4k per robot per year in support contracts, refurbished-unit sales, and escrow and trustee fees.
non_obvious_insight: In every hardware boom the durable second-derivative business is keeping the losers' machines running. Buyers pay to avoid stranded assets, and your spares moat grows with each vendor that fails.
first_30_days: Identify 3 wound-down or struggling robot vendors, get trustee quotes on inventory (often pennies on the dollar), and approach their 5 largest customers. Sign 2 support contracts and open a small depot near Memphis or the Inland Empire.

title: Turf-Ban Pivot Desk for Lawn and Irrigation Crews
one_liner: A done-for-you back office that turns lawn-maintenance crews into rebate-financed turf-removal and drip-conversion contractors, and uses their weekly routes as a cheap verification network for water utilities.
customer: Independent lawn-care, landscape-maintenance and irrigation companies with 5-40 crew members in drought-restricted Western and Texas metros. Secondary payers are water utilities and conservation funders.
problem: Their core product, mowing and irrigating turf, is being restricted and priced out as drought and utility rules spread. The replacement product (turf removal, drip conversion, native planting) is a project business with estimating, permits, rebate paperwork (pre-inspection photos, invoices, post-inspection) and financing, and national outfits are taking the work. Getting customers is small firms' #1 operational challenge in the Fed's 2026 survey, and legacy local-marketing vendors like Thryv are shrinking.
solution: A rebate-stacking engine per address (utility, county, state, supplier), net-cost-after-rebate estimates, photo-guided pre and post documentation, and submission with follow-up. Bridge financing against assigned rebates. Auto-generated local landing pages, Google Business Profile posts and mailers to the crew's existing maintenance clients ('your street qualifies for $X'). A route-verification add-on where crews photo-confirm turf has stayed removed so utilities can count the savings.
why_now: 49.6% of the US is in drought and the Colorado River 2027-2036 framework forces cuts. $7.2B of FY2026 SRF money is flowing. Corporate water-positive money, such as Amazon's $20M into the Water Resilience Coalition, increasingly needs verified savings that can be counted. Lower-cost LLM tooling makes per-address rebate rules and local pages cheap to produce for a 10-person crew.
revenue_model: 10% of rebate dollars processed (rebates on a job commonly run from several hundred to a few thousand dollars). 2% per month on bridge advances. $199/mo marketing add-on. $25-$60 per site per year from utilities or funders for route verification.
non_obvious_insight: The crew's client list and weekly route are the real assets. They are the only workforce already at every yard every week, which makes them both the best sales channel for turf conversion and a near-zero-cost inspection network to catch re-sodding, the thing utilities and funders need before they trust rebate savings. The subsidy is a sales script, not the product.
first_30_days: Pick one metro with a large turf rebate program. Find 5 lawn companies through the local green-industry association. Process 10 of their pending rebates free, then charge 10%. Publish a 'net cost after rebates' page for each crew's service area. Pitch one utility on a paid route-verification pilot covering 200 sites.

title: Waze for Agents: Live Bureaucracy Route Data
one_liner: A pay-per-lookup feed of the current, tested state of consumer and government web procedures (form changes, outages, hidden requirements, real step timings), sold to browser agents just before they attempt an errand.
customer: Browser and computer-use agents, and the agent platforms that run them, paying $0.005-$0.10 per route lookup via x402 or MPP. The heaviest users will be agents doing errands: license renewals, permits, benefits applications, insurance claims, utility transfers, refunds.
problem: Procedure websites change weekly with no changelog. Every failed attempt burns tokens, and worse, can leave a half-finished irreversible state such as a submitted but unpaid renewal. Every agent relearns the same breakages, and nobody pools that knowledge.
solution: Two data engines. First, synthetic canaries: daily automated dry-runs of the top ~500 US flows (state DMV and DOL, county property tax, SSA/IRS/USCIS account setup, top utilities, top insurers' claim portals, airline refund forms). They record schema diffs, required documents, CAPTCHAs, session timeouts and upload limits, and publish step-by-step 'route cards' with a success rate and freshness timestamp. Second, opt-in failure telemetry from customer agents, traded for credits, which covers the long tail Waze-style. Customers get a 'route guarantee': if a route verified in the last 24 hours fails, the lookup is refunded.
why_now: Browser agents moved from demo to production in 2026, with vendors reporting thousands of automated workflows per week on legacy portals. x402 and MPP make $0.01 lookups collectable without accounts. Governments are still not publishing agent-readable metadata.
revenue_model: Metered lookups, plus $500-$5,000/month platform plans for agent vendors that include telemetry credits. Premium verified-fresh routes for high-stakes flows, and later aggregate breakage analytics sold to agencies who want to fix their own forms.
non_obvious_insight: For an agent the scarce input is not information but freshness plus negative results: knowing what broke this morning. Agents' own failures are the raw material, so each new customer improves the map, a data network effect a static scraper cannot copy. Government sites are the one part of the web nobody will ever optimize for agents, which keeps the drift problem permanent.
first_30_days: Write 50 Playwright canaries for the 10 highest-traffic flows in 5 large states, using a cheap model to diff DOM and field schemas. Publish a free MCP server and a public 'status page for bureaucracy' to draw agent builders. Offer free credits to 5 browser-agent startups in exchange for telemetry, and start charging in month 3 once the route guarantee has a track record.

title: Playable-Until Guarantees for Online Games
one_liner: Sell publishers a pre-funded shutdown trust plus an escrowed server kit, so a dated playability guarantee becomes a selling point for $70-80 online games instead of a legal risk.
customer: Indie and mid-size publishers (10-300 staff) of co-op and live-service titles on Steam and console, and premium online games priced at $70-80.
problem: Publishers treat any end-of-life promise as a liability admission, so buyers get none. Anthem shut down on 2026-01-12, and of 738 tracked shutdown games 68% are unplayable or at risk. The EU Commission declined a mandatory rule on 2026-06-16 but wants a voluntary code by end of 2026. UFC-Que Choisir sued Ubisoft over The Crew, and a suit against Sony followed in Aug 2026.
solution: A 'Last Light' package with three parts. (1) Escrow of a server-emulator kit, builds and docs, verified by a clean-room restore drill we run. (2) A small per-title trust funded at launch (1-2% of gross) that pays a hosting partner to keep a minimal community server up for N years. (3) A store-page badge with a date, plus a public verification page. If a sunset trigger fires, the kit is released to the community.
why_now: The EU voluntary code of conduct due by end of 2026 will set a de facto standard that needs an auditor. The Stop Killing Games petition has 1.29M verified signers, a ready-made audience. $70-80 pricing needs a value story, and the Ubisoft and Sony suits show the cost of staying silent.
revenue_model: Certification and restore-drill fee of $8-40k per title, 15-20% admin retention on trust contributions, and $3-5k annual re-certification.
non_obvious_insight: A bounded, dated, funded promise caps liability, while silence leaves it open-ended and now litigated. Most online games reduce to stateless auth and matchmaking, so the guarantee is cheap to keep. Publishers also get a marketing asset that the Stop Killing Games community will actively promote.
first_30_days: Recruit volunteer engineers from the Stop Killing Games community to draft a reference escrow spec. Pitch 30 indie co-op publishers with launches in the next 12 months. Run a free restore drill on one willing title and publish it as a case study. Presell 3 pilots at $5-8k, and get a hosting-partner letter of intent and a lawyer-reviewed template.

title: Safety Compliance-as-a-Service for Robot Deployments
one_liner: A standing team plus software that produces the risk assessments, safety validation and insurer paperwork every facility needs before deploying AMRs, cobots or humanoid pilots.
customer: EHS and operations directors at mid-size 3PLs, manufacturers and food or cold-storage plants, integrators without in-house safety staff, and insurers who want documentation.
problem: Deployments stall at safety sign-off. ISO 10218 was revised in 2025, standards for dynamically stable robots and humanoids are still being written, integrators are overloaded, and insurers and OSHA ask for documented assessments. Amazon's 1M-robot scale keeps injury scrutiny high.
solution: Field engineers plus templated software: site scan, risk assessment against current standards, laser-scanner zone and e-stop validation, speed-and-separation testing, training records and incident logs, with annual recertification. Offer a premium 'humanoid pilot safety case' product.
why_now: Humanoid pilots are moving into real facilities in 2026 (Figure reports about 350 units delivered, Agility has a $300M+ single-customer order) while standards lag. Insurers are starting to require paperwork, so it is a channel as well as a service.
revenue_model: $8-25k per site assessment, $3-8k a year for recertification, and software seats for integrators.
non_obvious_insight: For many humanoid and AMR pilots the true bottleneck is one safety officer's signature, and almost no independent practitioners exist. Insurers will steer clients to whoever produces accepted documentation, which gives you distribution.
first_30_days: Recruit a certified functional-safety engineer as cofounder and build assessment templates. Sell 3 fixed-price assessments at about $10k each from integrators' backlogs, and publish a free humanoid pilot safety checklist to generate inbound.
